A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Annealed Q-learning study. All 20 pages, including Appendices A–J, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original tabular MDP experiments, DM Control and Meta-World evaluations, and supplementary experiments on annealing, estimation bias, exploration and stochasticity.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their numerical and graphical results in the main text and Appendices A–J.

M1.justification: The expectile critic objective, linear annealing schedule, TD3/SAC integrations and appendix variants are unchanged. Section 5's added wording about maximization under the current policy restates the action sampling already specified in v1 Section 3.4 and Equation 6.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same preliminary MDP, 10 DM Control locomotion tasks and 10 single-task Meta-World manipulation tasks. The appendix scenarios involving modified rewards, injected noise and stochastic hopper-hop are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: TD3, SAC and XQL in the main DM Control comparison, and TD3 and SAC in Meta-World. The appendix max-backup and other variant comparisons are retained. The expanded discussion of Ji et al. (2024) adds no evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the main training budgets of 3 million DM Control steps and 10 million Meta-World steps, batch size 256, two 256-unit hidden layers, evaluation metrics and annealing settings. Supplementary experimental protocols also match.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and the appendices retain the same analyses of fixed versus annealed expectiles, noise and reward sensitivity, annealing duration and shape, extended training, V-function use, estimation bias, exploration and MXQL. No analysis or supporting evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix B specifies the same 10 random seeds for DM Control and 5 for Meta-World. Confidence intervals, plotted uncertainty bands and the policy-entropy table's uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted curves match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains mean returns of 740.3 for AQ-TD3 and 746.1 for AQ-SAC at 3 million steps. Appendix score tables, entropy measurements and qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The Bellman operator definitions, expectile formulation, Jensen's inequality argument for overestimation, update and annealing equations, and Appendix A policy-gradient expressions are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about faster learning, reduced late-training bias, improved performance and robustness to optimality-related hyperparameters. The abstract's code-availability sentence relocates existing information.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the learning-speed/bias tradeoff, exploration benefits, stochasticity experiments and annealing behavior are unchanged. Existing qualifications about sensitivity and future optimization of annealing schedules are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation details and hyperparameters, including those in Appendices A, B and J, are unchanged. The identical code-repository link moves from the end of the introduction to the abstract; no new resource or access instruction is disclosed.

R1.justification: Section 5 makes the comparison with Ji et al. (2024) more explicit: their in-sample maximization uses replay-buffer actions, whereas AQ-L uses the current policy. This modestly sharpens the methodological positioning. The cited works and broader relationship to prior research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: the code sentence moves into the abstract, the closest-prior-work paragraph gains explanatory wording, and five bibliography URLs are removed while their references remain. Section organization and nearly all prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: The relocated code sentence and related-work/reference edits cause limited text reflow on the opening and bibliography pages. All figures and tables retain their content, captions, structure and placement; the rendered appendix pages are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity by explicitly contrasting replay-buffer maximization with current-policy maximization in the closest-prior-work discussion. Moving the existing code link into the abstract also improves its visibility. Removing several bibliography URLs slightly reduces navigation convenience, but the references remain identifiable. The scientific evidence and reproducibility details are unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
